analysis:
Examined the changes in ProviderLoop+Preload.swift and ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift.

Preload.swift (line 30): the load_model gate changes from autopilotAllowsModel to autopilotServesModel. The definition is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot tell whether the new predicate is stricter or looser. It still fails closed with model_not_selected, and the other gates are unchanged: autopilotManagesResidency, runtime eligibility, shutdown, revision update and drain. Line 119 only widens finishPreloadTask from private to internal. It is still guarded by the taskId match at line 125, so a caller needs the correct UUID; no new remote surface is visible, but the new internal callers are not shown.

StartupPreload.swift: canLoadMore now also requires !startupPreloadStopRequested (patch, around line 310). The flag is reset in finishStartupPreload (around line 306). The change can only stop the driver from starting further loads, so it narrows work rather than widening it. A stale flag after a stop is not a security issue. Where the flag is set, and the superviseTransitions logic it refers to, are outside the supplied files. The change does not touch the registration gate, the shutdown cancel path, or the attestation/App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053).

No prompt data, key material, cache storage (T-041) or authorization semantics are altered in the visible diffs. Remaining integration questions: the semantic difference between autopilotServesModel and autopilotAllowsModel, so the model-selection control is not weakened; and the setter of startupPreloadStopRequested plus the new callers of finishPreloadTask, which sit in other files.
